index.title: Welcome to my site!
index.content:
Hey! I’m Matthew. I currently work as a Lead Product Manager at Field building out essential renewable energy infrastructure.
Previously, I’ve worked at Bulb and Cuckoo.
I think about technology, software, team/company dynamics and productivity. In normal life you’ll catch me reading (Sci-Fi, Fantasy) or running/walking somewhere green and leafy.
Elsewhere you can find me on LinkedIn.

posts/Happiness-in-small-things.title: Happiness in small things
posts/Happiness-in-small-things.content:
Today I got a gift. It made me happy.
It wasn’t a large gift. It didn’t fill an impossibly deep hole in my existence. But it made me happy.
It was socks. It made me happy.
No it isn’t Christmas. I play regular football with a group from work and have been trudging out in the same pair of socks that I bought nearly 10 years ago playing 5-a-side at my first job out of university. Understandably, they were showing their age.
The colours, faded. The material, bobbly, irregular and with more holes than the regulation single hole.
It registered as a minor irritant. An irk. A slight shudder of embarrassment each week as they disappear into the laundry basket and sleep for a few days.
Hannah noticed. Noticed something she didn’t have to. It needn’t have registered. When we care, we notice things beyond what is required or asked of us.
That thought, that made me happy.

posts/The-second-best-time-is-right-now.title: The second best time is right now
posts/The-second-best-time-is-right-now.content:
“The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago. The second best is now.”

Supposedly this comes from “an old Chinese proverb”. Some basic internet digging suggests this came into common usage in the 1960s (as prompted by someone equally suspicious about putting any vaguely wise-sounding soundbites in the “ancient Chinese wisdom” bucket too quickly.
In any case, the sentiment holds.
I’ve been meaning to write more for a little while now. And then once you’ve written a thing why not share it? Not with expectation. Not because everyone desperately needs to hear what I have to say.
I’m sharing because:

It increases the chance that someone might read a thing that I write and share something that makes the next thing better.
Someone might take an idea from what I’ve written and find it helpful or interesting (maybe both?)

I have to credit the written word of Russell Davies - who recently released Do interesting & Giles Turnbull - author of The agile comms handbook - as a gentle shove in this direction.
I don’t (yet) have a topic or focus to what I’ll write here. Let’s see what emerges.
